title: HTS assay validation: plate uniformity and Z' factor
summary: NCATS Assay Guidance Manual procedure for proving an assay is screen-ready: run Max, Mid and Min control plates across several days, compute CV, signal window and Z', check drift and edge effects, then compare potencies across runs.

steps.text: Choose a plate layout: interleaved Max/Mid/Min signals (three plates per day) or a dose-response-plus-uniform-signal layout.
Run the uniformity study for 3 days for a new assay, 2 days for an assay transfer.
Read the plates on the intended detection platform.
Check CV of Max and Mid signals is 20% or less, signal window at least 2, and drift/edge effects below 20%.
Compute Z' = 1 - 3(SD_max + SD_min)/|mean_max - mean_min| and require at least 0.4 (0.5+ preferred for HTS).
Run a replicate-experiment study with 20-30 compounds in two independent runs; require minimum significant ratio below 3.

materials: Control reagents (Max, Mid, Min), reference compounds

source.publisher: NCBI Bookshelf, Assay Guidance Manual (NCATS/Eli Lilly)

notes: Authors/year are from our knowledge of the chapter, not shown in the fetched text. Thresholds (Z' 0.4, MSR<3) are as stated in the chapter; pipeline text uses 0.5 as conventional. Source authors and year not recorded: they were not confirmed from the opened page.
